AnyCalib.output_convention: intrinsics already mapped back to ORIGINAL image pixels by predict(); [fx, fy, cx, cy, k1, k2] for radial:2; normalised radial polynomial 1 + k1 r^2 + k2 r^4 (OpenCV-compatible)

GeoCalib.checkpoint_release: GitHub release v1.0, fetched by the package itself via torch.hub.load_state_dict_from_url
GeoCalib.output_convention: camera.f already in original pixels; principal point fixed at the image centre and reported as NOT_PREDICTED; radial k1,k2 OpenCV-compatible
GeoCalib.critical_pin: kornia==0.7.2 (newer kornia has a TorchScript incompatibility with torch 2.1.2)

PerspectiveFields.commit_resolution: installed from a local clone at experiments/cache/external_models/PerspectiveFields; commit read from that clone's git HEAD
PerspectiveFields.output_convention: rel_focal = f / image_height; f_px = rel_focal * H
PerspectiveFields.install_note: installed with --no-deps; albumentations pulls stringzilla which has no Windows wheel and is not needed for inference

AnyCam.commit_resolution: git rev-parse HEAD of the clone at experiments/cache/external_models/anycam, made during the CAM-EXP-004.1 static applicability audit
AnyCam.windows_blocker: anycam/scripts/fit_video.py applies torch.compile at import, which raises 'Windows not yet supported for torch.compile' on torch <= 2.5; meanwhile the UniDepth depth backbone imports xformers.components.attention.NystromAttention, which exists only in xformers <= 0.0.28.post3 - a version with no Windows wheel that also requires torch 2.5.1. The two requirements are mutually exclusive on this platform, and satisfying them would require editing official source, which was not done.
AnyCam.code_path_of_the_identifiability_test: the same functions anycam/scripts/fit_video.py uses to score its 32 focal candidates before proj_labels.argmax(); called unmodified on synthetic depth with identity vs translating relative poses

checkpoint_source.resolved_from: the repository's own hubconf.py, which downloads config.yaml and pytorch_model.bin from that repo id

AnyCam.benchmark_status: NOT_A_PERFORMANCE_BENCHMARK - AnyCam was never run as a ranked baseline and produced no focal-accuracy number
AnyCam.status: NOT_APPLICABLE_REQUIRES_CAMERA_MOTION - the official focal selection objective is flat across all 32 candidates under a static camera (spread 2.73e-09 vs 0.223 with camera motion)

note: AnyCalib and GeoCalib exact commits were recovered from pip's direct_url.json; no EXACT_COMMIT_UNRESOLVED_FOR_HISTORICAL_RUN case remained, so no re-install equivalence check was needed for provenance reasons. An independent equivalence check on the 8 shared frames is reported separately.
